chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The dry suweeq (flour soup) removes the whiteness (vitiligo).

key_terms.السَّوِيقُ: A traditional food made from roasted flour mixed with water or milk.
key_terms.الْبَيَاضُ: Whiteness, specifically referring to vitiligo (a skin condition causing loss of color).
key_terms.الْجَافُّ: Dry, as opposed to wet or freshly mixed.

ai.seo_question: What is the medicinal benefit of dry suweeq according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the therapeutic efficacy of dry *suweeq* (a porridge of flour, water, and milk) for treating vitiligo, reflecting the Prophetic tradition of utilizing simple, accessible foods for healing. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on *al-tibb al-nabawi* (Prophetic medicine), where dietary habits are viewed not merely for sustenance but as means to restore physical balance and treat specific ailments.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yahya Bin Al Mubarak, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The dry Al-Suweyq does away with the whiteness (vitiligo?)’.
